pageTitle: Write and Solve Equations Using Addition or Subtraction
covers: how to solve one-step addition and subtraction equations by doing the same inverse operation to both sides, and how to check the answer

intro.caption: Lesson 8-2 — solving addition and subtraction equations. The Big Balance is Screamline Park's favorite ride: two cars on a long beam. When both sides weigh the same, it swings smooth and level. Today it is badly tipped, and Rafi is the only ride tech on duty.

balloons.t: The ride is lopsided. Level it. NO refunds!
A balance ride is just an equation with seats.
My side is way down. Is it the mascot head? It's the head, isn't it.
Quick fix: I'll ADD sandbags to Gus's side. Wait. That makes it worse.

pages.caption: Adding weight to only one side tips the ride even more. To keep an equation balanced, do the same thing to both sides.

balloons.t: Whatever leaves one side must leave the other.

pages.caption: Left car: a mystery crate x and 12 sandbags. Right car: 30 sandbags. The ride is level, so x + 12 = 30.

balloons.t: Adding undoes taking away. Taking away undoes adding. Even raccoons know that.
Those are inverse operations. Use the one that undoes what is stuck to the letter.
My booth too! I had some prizes. I gave away 14. I have 29 left.
Write it, then isolate the letter. Get it alone on one side.

pages.ch: Boss Gate · The Last Three Loads

balloons.t: Three last loads. If it tips, no funnel cake for you.
Sir, I get paid in funnel cake!
Level ride. Now level my funnel cake supply.

win.caption: To solve an addition or subtraction equation, use the inverse operation on both sides: subtract to undo adding, add to undo subtracting. Then check by putting the answer back in.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Keep It Level
gates.prompt: The ride shows x + 12 = 30. Rafi wants the crate x alone in the left car, and the ride must stay level.
hints: Conceptual: the ride is level because both sides weigh the same. Change only one side and it tips.
Procedural: take the 12 sandbags off the left car. Then ask: what must happen to the right car so the ride stays level?

steps: Practice ride: x + 5 = 14. Five bags sit next to the crate.
Take 5 bags off the left. Take 5 bags off the right too: 14 − 5 = 9.
The crate is alone and the ride is level: x = 9.
worked.q: Practice ride x + 8 = 20. Take 8 off both sides. What is x?

items.q: Rafi takes 12 sandbags off the left car. What must he do to keep the ride level?

options.t: Nothing — only the left car changed
options.fb: Changing only one side tips the ride. The left lost 12, so the right must lose 12 too.

options.t: Add 12 sandbags to the right car
options.fb: Adding to the right makes it even heavier. The left LOST 12, so the right must lose 12.

options.t: Take 12 sandbags off the right car too
Take all 30 sandbags off the right car
options.fb: Then the right car is empty and the crate's side drops. Take off the same amount: 12.

items.label: After taking 12 off both sides, x =
items.aria: weight of the crate x after taking 12 off both sides

fb.msg: That's 30 + 12. You added to the right side instead of taking 12 away.
That changed only the left side. Take 12 off the right side too.

items.fbDefault: The right side had 30. Take 12 away from it.

gates.pass: 30 − 12 = 18. The crate weighs 18 bags, and the beam doesn't wobble. Gus's car rises. Gus screams anyway.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Undo It
gates.prompt: Each load has a number stuck to the letter. Pick the inverse operation that undoes it, on both sides.
hints: Conceptual: adding and subtracting undo each other. To undo − 9, add 9. To undo + 27, subtract 27.
Procedural: look at the sign in front of the number next to the letter. Do the opposite to BOTH sides.

steps: Practice: a − 6 = 10. The 6 is subtracted from a.
The inverse of subtracting 6 is adding 6. Add 6 to both sides: a = 10 + 6.

options.fb: The 27 is already added to m. Adding another 27 does not undo it. Subtract it.

options.t: Subtract 27 from the left side only
options.fb: Changing only one side tips the ride. Subtract 27 from BOTH sides.
Dividing undoes multiplying. Here 27 is ADDED to m, so subtract it.

items.label: Solve y − 9 = 16. y =
items.aria: value of y in y minus 9 equals 16

fb.msg: That's 16 − 9. Subtracting again does not undo − 9. Add 9 to both sides.
You dropped the 9 from one side only. Add 9 to both sides: 16 + 9.

items.fbDefault: The 9 is subtracted from y. Add 9 to both sides.

gates.pass: Subtract to undo adding, add to undo subtracting: y = 25. Bandit nods like he taught them.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Solve the Loads
gates.prompt: Solve each equation. Isolate the letter, then check by putting your answer back in.
hints: Conceptual: isolate means get the letter alone. Undo the number next to it with the inverse operation.
Procedural: subtract to undo +, add to undo −, on both sides. Then substitute to check that both sides match.

steps: Practice: c + 13 = 40. The 13 is added to c.

items.label: A load on the ride: h + 17 = 41. h =
items.aria: value of h in h plus 17 equals 41

fb.msg: That's 41 + 17. Adding does not undo + 17. Subtract 17 from both sides. Check: 58 + 17 is 75, not 41.
You took the 17 off only one side. Subtract 17 from 41 too.

items.fbDefault: Subtract 17 from both sides, then check: your answer + 17 should be 41.

items.label: Hana's booth: p − 14 = 29. How many prizes did she start with? p =
items.aria: number of prizes Hana started with

fb.msg: That's 29 − 14. Subtracting does not undo − 14. Add 14 to both sides. Check: 15 − 14 is 1, not 29.
29 is what she has LEFT. She started with more. Add the 14 she gave away.

items.fbDefault: She gave 14 away. Add 14 to both sides to find what she started with.

gates.pass: h = 24 and p = 43. Checks: 24 + 17 = 41 and 43 − 14 = 29. Hana restocks her shelf.

gates.title: Boss Gate · The Last Three Loads
gates.prompt: Three loads before the ride opens. Solve each one and keep both sides equal.
hints: Conceptual: whatever you do to one side, do to the other. The inverse of adding is subtracting, and the inverse of subtracting is adding.
Procedural: find the number next to the letter, do the opposite operation to both sides, then substitute to check.

steps: Practice: 52 = e + 19. The letter can be on either side.
Subtract 19 from both sides: 52 − 19 = 33, so e = 33.

items.label: Load 1 · x + 38 = 75. x =
items.aria: value of x in x plus 38 equals 75

fb.msg: That's 75 + 38. You added instead of subtracting. Undo + 38 by subtracting 38.

items.fbDefault: Subtract 38 from both sides, then check your answer.

items.label: Load 2 · w − 26 = 19. w =
items.aria: value of w in w minus 26 equals 19

fb.msg: That's 19 − 26. Subtracting again does not undo − 26. Add 26 to both sides.
That's 26 − 19. Undo − 26 by adding 26 to both sides: 19 + 26.

items.fbDefault: Add 26 to both sides, then check: your answer − 26 should be 19.

items.q: Load 3 · Gus solves k + 8 = 20 and writes k = 28. What is right?

options.fb: Check it: 28 + 8 = 36, not 20. Gus added 8 instead of subtracting it.
Dropping the 8 from one side changes only that side. Check: 20 + 8 is 28, not 20.
Multiplying does not undo adding. Subtract 8 from both sides.

gates.pass: x = 37, w = 45, k = 12. The Big Balance swings smooth and level. Mr. Krank puts away the refund forms.

journal.heading: Lesson 8-2 — what the balance ride taught us
rows: An equation is a level ride. Do the same thing to both sides and it stays level.
Subtract to undo adding. Add to undo subtracting. In x + 12 = 30, subtract 12 from both sides: x = 18.
Get the letter alone. In p − 14 = 29, add 14 to both sides: p = 43.
Put the answer back in. 43 − 14 = 29, so p = 43 is the solution.
Adding sandbags to one side only made it worse. Change both sides, and undo with the opposite operation.
journal.quote: "Two pieces of funnel cake, one in each paw. That is balance. That is life." — Bandit

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 8-2 (Write and Solve Equations Using Addition or Subtraction) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: keeping an equation balanced, inverse operations for addition and subtraction, solving one-step equations, and checking by substitution.
standards: Understand solving an equation as a process of answering which values make it true; solve one-step addition and subtraction equations using inverse operations
